entries.title: Enforce password history (remember 24 passwords)
entries.description: Sets the account password-history length to 24 so a user cannot immediately reuse a recent password.
entries.rationale: Remembering 24 passwords, combined with a minimum password age, prevents users from cycling straight back to a favourite password after a forced change. CIS Windows 11 Benchmark 1.1.1.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Enforce password history

sideEffects: Only meaningful for local accounts; Microsoft-account and Azure AD sign-ins are governed by their own identity provider.

entries.title: Set a minimum password age of 1 day
entries.description: Requires a password to be at least one day old before it can be changed again.
entries.rationale: Without a minimum age a user can change their password 24 times in a row to flush the password history and return to the original password. One day defeats that while staying invisible in normal use. CIS Windows 11 Benchmark 1.1.3.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Minimum password age

sideEffects: A user who genuinely needs to change a just-changed password must wait a day or have an administrator reset it.

entries.title: Require a minimum password length of 14
entries.description: Sets the minimum length for local-account passwords to 14 characters.
entries.rationale: Fourteen characters is the long-standing CIS/Microsoft baseline minimum and makes offline password cracking dramatically harder. CIS Windows 11 Benchmark 1.1.4.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Minimum password length

sideEffects: Applies at the next password change; existing shorter passwords keep working until then. Users who prefer short passwords will have to choose a longer one.
Only affects local accounts; it does not change the password rules of a Microsoft or Azure AD account.

entries.title: Require password complexity
entries.description: Enables the built-in password-complexity requirement (mix of character classes, not based on the account name).
entries.rationale: Complexity requirements block the weakest passwords (the user name, single-class passwords) and are part of every recognised Windows hardening baseline. CIS Windows 11 Benchmark 1.1.5.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Password Policy\Password must meet complexity requirements

sideEffects: Applies at the next password change. Users must choose passwords with mixed character classes; consider a passphrase policy alongside this.

entries.title: Lock accounts after 5 failed sign-ins
entries.description: Locks a local account for 15 minutes after 5 failed sign-in attempts, counting failed attempts over a 15-minute window (LockoutBadCount, LockoutDuration and ResetLockoutCount).
entries.rationale: An account-lockout threshold turns online password guessing into a slow, noisy attack. Windows 11 now enables a 10/10/10 lockout by default; 5 attempts with a 15-minute lockout and 15-minute reset window is the CIS Level 1 baseline. CIS Windows 11 Benchmark 1.2.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Account Policies\Account Lockout Policy

sideEffects: A user (or an administrator) who mistypes a password 5 times is locked out for 15 minutes; there is no local-console exemption, so keep an alternative administrative access path.
The lockout threshold is set first so the duration and reset window can be applied; revert restores each captured prior value in reverse order.
